To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the improvement parameter gamma(*) in lattice Hamiltonian systems is a nonuniversal quantity, (ii) it depends on the lattice action, the lattice spacing, the lattice dimension, and the number of components of the vector spin, and (iii) the improvement is a nonperturbative effect.
the improvement parameter is gamma=0 in the O(2) and O(3) cases and gamma=2/3 in the O(4) case.

the improvement parameter gamma(*) of the lattice Hamiltonian in the vector spin model is given by (N-2)/N, that the critical region of the Hamiltonian is defined by the condition gamma>gamma(*) and that the leading nonscaling contributions to renormalization group invariant physical quantities vanish in the critical region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the improvement parameter gamma* of the lattice Hamiltonian for vector spin models with an O(N) symmetry in the framework of the 1/N expansion method.
the following topics: 1) Evaluation of the improvement parameter gamma* in lattice Hamiltonian systems. 2) Systematic asymptotic expansions for lattice massive one-loop diagrams.

the following problems: (a) the determination of the critical value gamma* of the coupling constant for which the leading irrelevant operator is absent in the lattice Hamiltonians for vector spin models with a quartic interaction; (b) the evaluation of the leading nonscaling contributions to physical quantities in the critical region, for the lattice Hamiltonians of vector spin models; and (c) the determination of systematic asymptotic expansions of the one-loop massive integrals for lattice Hamiltonian models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the lattice Hamiltonians of vector spin models, the improvement parameter is always well defined, and that the leading irrelevant operator always decouples at a critical value of gamma.
, in the framework of the 1/N expansion, there is no evidence that the leading irrelevant operator is decoupled for any N.
, in the case of the O(N) model, the improvement parameter gamma(*) is not universal, but depends on the number of components N.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for the O(2) model in two dimensions, the leading irrelevant operator is irrelevant in the sense that the corresponding coupling constant is irrelevant in the RG sense, and that the corresponding contribution to the critical specific heat is of order 1/N.
the lattice Hamiltonian is a powerful tool in studying critical phenomena, but its use is limited to a small class of lattice systems with quartic coupling constants.
, in the case of the lattice Hamiltonian for vector models, the improvement parameter gamma(*) can be evaluated exactly and is equal to zero.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the improvement parameter is a nonuniversal quantity.
the leading irrelevant operator does not decouple for the lattice Hamiltonians considered.
the improvement parameter gamma(*) is not an expansion parameter in the 1/N expansion and that, therefore, it is not possible to use this parameter to improve the accuracy of 1/N expansions.
